_comment: SPOTS THAT KEEP THEIR OWN HRRR CELL WHEN HRRR COUNTS IT AS LAND. Read by
pipeline/forecast/hrrr.py (load_land_cell_spots). Every other spot whose nearest HRRR cell
is land reads the nearest seaward water cell instead (#276): at an exposed beach the air
reaching the lineup has come over water, and the land cell is HRRR slowing it over its own
land surface. These spots sit in the lee of a headland or in a cove, where the water cell,
out beyond the headland, overstates the wind the lineup feels.
Decided 2026-10-22 from data-quality run 41: every hour the water cell cost a spot 1.5
stars or more was reviewed spot by spot. The calls are geographic judgment, not checked
against observed wind; validating land vs water wind against coastal observations
(NDBC C-MAN or similar) at a few of these spots is on the backlog.
Keyed by slug (the name lower-cased, non-alphanumerics to '-'); the value is the reason.

spots.trinidad-state-beach: Between Trinidad Head and Elk Head (CA); the water cell, 2.8 km WSW beyond both, read 20-26 kt in N wind where the land cell read 13-15 kt.
spots.indian-beach-ecola: A cove under Tillamook Head (OR), sheltered from N-NW wind; land 5-11 kt against water 17-23 kt in run 41.
spots.la-push-third-beach: A south-facing cove between Taylor Point and Teahwhit Head (WA); NW wind reaches it offshore over forested headland.
spots.cannon-beach: Reads the same land and water cells as Indian Beach Ecola, so its point sits at the north end under Ecola Point (OR).
spots.bastendorff-beach: Tucked behind the Coos Bay south jetty and Coos Head (OR), with shelter from north wind.
